pcs.pc_description: Obtain order details such as transport plans, delivery schedules, priority orders, daily work allocation, etc. and develop daily work plan factoring in priority cases, cases requiring exceptional handling
Get the work plan approved by the manager and arrange for daily shipment processing and quoting
Allocate tasks and resources to workers, drivers and associates
Address any disruptions during the day, such as vehicle breakdowns, accidents, or late deliveries.
Track the progress of deliveries and ensure that they are on schedule.
Ensure that all drivers have clear assignments for the day and that they are equipped with the necessary information (route details, delivery times, etc.).
Supervise deployment of cargoes in communication with the consignee's supervisor
Supervise loading, unloading, lashing and securing shipments for transport.
Coordinate with other departments to plan the movement of transport
Track fuel usage, monitor vehicle maintenance schedules, and ensure that vehicles are checked regularly to avoid unnecessary breakdowns.
Take note of the pending tasks in each activity to plan for the next day and plan for additional resources if required
Measure and document processes as per productivity standards
Liaise with officials and external stakeholders to streamline operations.
Assist in resolving freight-related billing/documentation issues and carrier performance-related issues and escalate to the manager if required.
Feed regular updates into ERP and send regular reports to the manager
Track performance metrics, such as on-time deliveries, fuel consumption, driver performance, and incidents.
Check for the selection of the type of truck required based on load carriage, route, load consolidation and associated costs
Cross-check details, including road permit, Commercial Driver's License (CDL), shipping bills, valid vehicle documents, etc., are correctly captured and verified by associates
Check for the presence of permits and regulatory compliances for operating articulated vehicles, reefer vehicles, trailers, trucks, etc.
Supervise and approve driver deployment

Use software tools such as FMS/ Telematics or GPS systems to identify the fastest and most fuel-efficient routes for drivers, considering factors like traffic, road conditions, time of day, and delivery windows.
Prioritise deliveries based on customer requirements, deadlines, or criticality.
Review and approve route plans for vehicles
Ensure that planned routes comply with transportation laws (weight limits, road restrictions, environmental laws, etc.).
Anticipate potential disruptions such as road closures, weather conditions, or accidents and Plan alternative routes in case of delays.
Adjust the routes in real-time in case of unforeseen delays or traffic conditions and communicate any necessary changes to drivers.

pcs.pc_description: Review transport schedule and booking records with reference to the plan
Verify that all drivers have valid and up-to- date commercial driver's licenses (CDLs) and any other certifications required by local or national regulations.

Ensure that all fleet vehicles are properly registered with the relevant authorities, including up-to-date registration certificates, permits, insurance, brake tests, emission controls, etc. and vehicle titles.
Examine lorry Receipt (LR), Goods Consignment (GC), transit insurance and tax permits for correctness and accuracy with respect to order
Check inbound documentation, freight invoices and signed agreements for any errors or discrepancies and resolve documentation problems, if any.
Review logs detailing routine maintenance, repairs, and any issues identified during inspections.
Ensure that the Delivery and transport Documentation, such as the Bill of Lading (BOL), Delivery Notes, Waybills, POD, etc., is in order.
Conduct regular audits of both documentation and operations to ensure compliance. This could be a monthly or quarterly review of vehicle and driver records, inspection reports, and permits.
Stay updated on local, regional, or national transportation regulations and keep drivers and workers informed to reduce the risk of non- compliance.
Regularly communicate with relevant regulatory bodies to clarify any questions about compliance, seek advice, and ensure the company adheres to industry best practices.
Document any incidents of non-compliance, whether related to drivers, vehicles, or cargo and take corrective action.
Obtain daily status of documents from executives and associates
Compile a list of undelivered shipments and contact consignees of undelivered shipments to arrange for alternate deliveries
Prepare daily operation reports in terms of cargo movement, total loading and unloading activities, resource utilisation, workforce deployment and other parameters as per organisational requirement
Report daily damage, Material Handling Equipment (MHE) repair requirements, accidents, transport delays, etc.

modules.module_title: Plan and prepare for marshaling of vehicles

pcs.pc_description: Determine the work allocation for marshalling using the traffic management plan
Wear the required personal protective equipment for marshalling duties.
Check if the area is clear and suitable for vehicle manoeuvring activities as per site safety demarcation arrangements and control measures
Establish a safe marshalling position and maintain an appropriate field of vision.
Confirm smooth and safe movement of vehicles in the designated area by directing trucks, forklifts, delivery vehicles, and any other machinery to their appropriate spots.
Ensure that hand signals, cones, traffic wands and approved communication methods are used to guide vehicles.
Confirm vehicles do not block emergency exits, gates, or pedestrian paths.
Ensure that all vehicles move at a safe speed within the premises. This is especially important in busy areas where pedestrians or workers may be present.

Check whether vehicles are parked in the correct spaces at a safe distance from each other as per the designated layout or plan for the site and whether over-dimensional or heavy vehicles are parked in appropriate spaces that can accommodate their size.
Optimise parking areas by coordinating with other marshals or workers to move vehicles around as necessary and ensure that all available spaces are used effectively.
Ensure that vehicles are correctly positioned for loading and unloading and that docks, ramps, or platforms are properly aligned.
Assist drivers in safely manoeuvring into position, if necessary, especially in tight spaces.
Ensure that vehicles are parked with adequate space to load/unload cargo without obstruction.
Supervise whether the Forklift or other material handling equipment has safe Vehicle Interaction to avoid accidents during the loading/unloading process.

Monitor whether Safety Protocols are followed, including whether drivers are wearing appropriate safety gear (e.g., hard hats and reflective vests), vehicles are not overloaded, cargo is properly secured, and vehicles are not parked in restricted areas or near hazardous materials.
Check for any safety hazards, such as oil spills, obstacles in the driving path, or unbalanced loads on vehicles that could pose a risk to the driver or other workers.

Assist in managing emergency situations like directing vehicles to safety, ensuring emergency vehicles have access to the area, Coordinating with safety officers or supervisors during evacuation or emergency situations etc.
Provide directions to drivers regarding Parking spots, loading/unloading areas, or restricted zones and ensure that they are aware of any hazards or specific site rules.
Report any delays, accidents, or incidents involving vehicles or drivers to the manager and ensure accurate documentation of incidents for future reference.
Stay in constant communication with other vehicle marshals or supervisors to ensure efficient operations and quick responses to any changes.

Coordinate emission testing inspection for trucks
Organise ordering/ purchasing of fuel, parts and supplies and maintain accurate inventory of equipment and spares
Track fleet usage and maintain an accurate inventory of equipment and spares
Create a comprehensive preventive maintenance plan for all vehicles based on manufacturer recommendations, vehicle age, usage, and operating conditions.
Ensure all vehicles undergo regular inspections and maintenance to avoid unexpected breakdowns.
Check past maintenance, repairs, and inspections for each vehicle in the fleet and maintenance records are up-to-date.
Monitor vehicle performance data such as engine diagnostics, fuel efficiency, and brake condition in real-time.
Ensure all vehicles are compliant with service requirements and can be assessed for any recurring issues.
Negotiate service agreements with vendors to ensure cost efficiency and Ensure that maintenance and repairs are done using quality materials
Evaluate vehicle inspection reports by Conducting routine checks on vehicles, including visual inspections and functional tests, to catch potential issues.
Document details of vehicle repair performed in the vehicle maintenance software program
Maintain daily purchase log and oil analysis book
Conduct price comparison research and maintain historical comparisons
Maintain record of fleet repairs, repair costs, parts procurement and vehicle warranties
Monitor maintenance expenses and track costs associated with repairs, parts, and labour.
Maintain trucks' out-of-service reports and inform operations staff and administration department of the status
Verify that all maintenance activities align with safety standards and legal requirements, such as emissions tests and vehicle inspections.
Prepare various reports (trucks out of service, fuel use, parts inventory, etc.) according to organisation guidelines and procedure
Analyse maintenance costs and provide recommendations on fleet utilisation and replacement
Regularly review fleet performance data to identify trends, such as higher-than-average maintenance costs or recurring mechanical problems.
Assist in the development of the fleet services budgets
Communicate maintenance requirements to the manager for budgetary approvals

pcs.pc_description: Use GPS and RFID (Radio Frequency Identification) tracking systems to monitor the location of goods in real-time.
Continuously update customers or stakeholders (warehouse teams, suppliers, etc.) on the status of consignments, especially if there are any delays or issues.
Ensure that consignments are delivered within the expected timeframes and compare actual delivery times with scheduled delivery windows to identify inefficiencies or delays.
Track the driver's route to ensure they are following the planned path, avoiding unnecessary detours, and adhering to scheduled stops for fuel, meals, or rest breaks.
Monitor conditions such as temperature and humidity through sensors to ensure that the consignment arrives in good condition if perishable goods or hazardous materials are transported.
Ensure that the goods are properly packaged and secured within the vehicle to prevent damage or theft during transit and track any issues related to cargo damage or safety concerns.

Handle delays and issues such as accidents, breakdowns, inordinate delays, or emergencies and take immediate action to resolve the problem, like rerouting the vehicle, notifying the customer, or making emergency arrangements.
Confirm that customers or recipients sign a delivery receipt, noting the condition of the goods upon arrival.
Keep track of vehicle availability, considering factors like maintenance schedules, driver schedules, and vehicle load capacity.
Ensure that drivers follow safety protocols, including speed limits, rest breaks, and use of seatbelts.
Use telematics or GPS to monitor vehicle speed, driving patterns, real-time updates, route changes, or assistance in case of road issues.
Ensure drivers complete pre-trip vehicle inspections before departing, including checking tyre pressure, fluid levels, and lights.
Ensure that vehicles are stocked with emergency supplies (e.g., first aid kits, spare tyres, and tools) and that drivers know what to do in case of breakdowns.
Set up alerts in the fleet management system to notify issues like low fuel, engine trouble, or unauthorised detours.
Ensure that the KPIs such as On-Time Delivery Rate, Fuel Efficiency, fewer vehicle Downtimes, Driver Safety Score, fewer damage Incidents, and Customer Satisfaction are met.

pcs.pc_description: Interpret the project requirements for transportation in terms of material involved, dimensions, weight, volume, etc.
Work out the loading and unloading requirements, lashing requirements based on the centre of gravity, stability required, etc.
Identify the timelines available for arranging the transportation.
Support design team by providing inputs on different types of lashing, trailer bed specification, load bearing capacity of axles, etc.
Select the routes that require surveying and arrange for the necessary documents, equipment, and tools (camera, GPS, tackles, etc.). to undertake the survey.
Drive on the selected route at posted speed.
Identify and describe critical points such as road conditions, traffic composition, water crossings, canals, overhead electric wires, residential areas, railway gate crossings, road hazards, etc.

Identify narrow roads, low bridges, sharp turns, culverts, and other obstacles that require removing, shifting, widening, construction of the bypass, etc., for safe transportation of ODC/ project cargo.
Evaluate the strength of bridges/culverts (bridge strength engineering calculations) for safe movement of heavy ODC.
Design bypass as per cargo specification for safe transportation.
Perform engineering lashing calculations to secure ODC onto the hydraulic trailer/barge/ship for safe transportation of heavy cargo.
Perform engineering calculations related to the movement of project cargo through sea/river.
Support route survey with photographs and identify major milestones.
Describe the route plan along with the schedule for transportation considering weather conditions during transit (rainy season, winter, fog, etc.)
Detail clear reasons along with photographs for the non-feasibility of a particular route for transportation.
Estimate the budgetary details, such as the cost of civil work en route, detailing the civil work at each different destination.
Conduct a feasibility study for the construction of the ro-ro jetty if required.
Conduct roll off and roll on calculations of load transfer from barge to shore and vice versa.
Perform route surveys in strict adherence to the safety and health standards and regulations.

Map the routes in the software application and load other details relating to road conditions, speed to be maintained at different sections of the route, stops, permit required, etc. and simulate the travel plan.
Arrange for specialised equipment, such as heavy lift cranes, to handle the cargo.
Determine the best mode/mix of modes for transporting the cargo based on the route survey analysis simulation and other information.
Determine the safest route for transport with the least transit time as per the route survey analysis.
Confirm the right vehicle for transportation according to the cargo, such as Flatbed Trucks, Lowboy Trailers, Self-Propelled Modular Transporters (SPMTs), etc.
Determine the total number of axles to be deployed for the transportation of heavy ODCs through engineering calculations.
Prepare the entire transport methodology, including the transport process, deployment of axles and load calculations, lashing method details, etc.
Identify storage, laydown areas, and handling points at both the pickup and delivery locations.
Prepare budgets for transportation, including workforce, consumables, fuel, civil works, road8diversions, permits, etc.
Discuss the travel plan & budget with the Manager and obtain concurrence.
Arrange good quality authorised drivers and trailer operators for successful project completion.
Prepare a detailed list of all permits to be received based on route survey inputs.
